newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER STEALS POLE FROM VILLENEUVE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER STEALS POLE FROM VILLENEUVE.

text.p: Michael Schumacher snatched pole position from home hope Jacques Villeneuve in the closing moments of Canadian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday.

Local hero Villeneuve had done his utmost to clock the fastest time and was quickest with only 30 seconds remaining. But it was not enough to prevent the double world champion upstaging him with a brilliant on-the-limit lap in his Ferrari.
Schumacher had headed the times twice before his last-gasp effort of one minute 18.095 seconds.
It was the German's first pole of the season, his and Ferrari's first since last year's Hungarian Grand Prix and the 15th of his career.
It also ended the Williams Renault team's run of 10 successive poles and dented their hopes of recording their 100th Formula One victory on Sunday.
Brazilian Rubens Barrichello was third best in his Stewart Ford after a magnificent effort in the closing five minutes.
Austrian debutant Alex Wurz crashed his Benetton into a wall late in the session but escaped unhurt.
Villeneuve's team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen was fourth quickest ahead of Briton David Coulthard in a McLaren and Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan.
